description: I'm a 10th-grade student interested in space exploration, storytelling, and creative technology. I enjoy researching, writing, and using computer tools to bring ideas to life. I attended the NASA Space Apps Challenge in person in San Jose, but due to low attendance, the event was moved online. I decided to continue independently and completed my project as a one-person team.
summary:
"Abandoned but Not Forgotten" is a short film about NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars.

The story follows Leo, a boy who feels discouraged about finishing a model rover he once built with his grandfather. During a magical journey through space, he discovers the stories of real spacecraft, rovers, and scientific instruments that helped us learn more about the universe.

By combining AI-generated images, storytelling, and real NASA images, this project brings attention to machines that are often overlooked after their missions end.

I hope the film inspires young people to appreciate space exploration and recognize how these machines, and the people behind them, helped make future discoveries possible.
details:
1. What does your project do, and how does it work?

My project is a short film that uses storytelling to introduce NASA equipment left behind on the Moon and Mars. It combines AI-generated images, authentic NASA photos and footage, narration, and sound effects to tell the stories of these machines, their missions, and their scientific contributions.

2. What benefits does your project have?

The film makes space history easier to understand and more interesting, especially for younger audiences. It helps viewers learn about NASA missions while recognizing the important achievements of equipment that is no longer in use.

3. What is the intended impact of your project?

I hope to inspire curiosity about space exploration and encourage people to appreciate the scientists, engineers, and machines that made important discoveries possible. I also want to show that even when a mission ends, its contributions can continue to influence future exploration.

4. What tools and software did you use?

  • Gemini: Research assistance and brainstorming.
  • ChatGPT: Image generation, script and dialogue reviews, and proofreading.
  • Suno AI: Music, sound effects, and soundtracks.
  • ElevenLabs: Character voices and narration.
  • Photopea: Image editing and visual effects.
  • Microsoft Clipchamp and CapCut: Video editing, transitions, and combining visuals with audio.

I developed the story, researched and selected the NASA equipment, wrote the script, designed the scenes, created and refined AI prompts, and edited the video while AI assisted with production.

5. How is your project creative?

Instead of making a traditional documentary, I created a fictional character, Leo, whose personal struggle connects to the idea of equipment being left behind. His magical journey allows viewers to discover real NASA history through an emotional story. I also combined AI-generated scenes with authentic NASA imagery to connect imagination with scientific facts.

6. What factors did you consider when developing your project?

I focused on scientific accuracy, making the story understandable for younger audiences, and balancing emotional storytelling with educational information. I also worked to keep the characters and settings visually consistent, accurately represent historical NASA equipment, and fit meaningful information into a short film.
